questions.prompt: Which arrangement matches the field layer of the hospital BMS?

options.text: Sensors and actuators are wired to field controllers
The BMS server is wired directly to every sensor without controllers
The corporate email server acts as each air-handling controller
Every lift connects only through the hospital web portal
A drawing alone replaces the physical field connections

questions.explanation: The chapter places sensors and actuators at the field layer, connected by wire to field controllers; the server belongs to the supervisory network.

questions.prompt: What does the chapter say a laptop that can reach classic BACnet/IP controllers may often do?

options.text: Read points and write setpoints without device authentication
Only read a public brochure about the controllers
Change setpoints only after a clinical diagnosis
Prove that a named person authorized every command
Automatically install secure protocol variants on all controllers

questions.explanation: Classic BACnet and Modbus deployments commonly trust network reachability; a laptop on the same network can usually read points and often write setpoints.

questions.prompt: Why is the dual-homed BMS-WS a critical meeting point?

options.text: It proves that every device is already compromised
It is disconnected from both the building and corporate networks
It joins corporate access with the building VLAN, creating a route to controllers
It eliminates all need for contractor remote access reviews
It changes the BACnet UDP port automatically

questions.explanation: The workstation has one interface on VLAN 300 and one on the corporate network; compromise can create a path into the controllers that zone design must address.

questions.prompt: Which set contains three meeting points the chapter asks analysts to consider?

options.text: Three different theatre temperature sensors
Only the chiller, its motor and its spare part
Only the BMS server and two printed drawings
A dual-homed workstation, contractor remote access and a lift cellular link
Only the three corporate email relays

questions.explanation: The text names a dual-homed BMS workstation, contractor support access and a lift manufacturer's cellular link as distinct routes between networks.

questions.prompt: How should Aisha map controller connectivity without risking older equipment?

options.text: Compare estates and contractor drawings with switch and firewall records; do not scan controllers
Run an unapproved network sweep against all field controllers
Treat a contractor drawing as proof of physical cabling
Ignore disagreements between the drawing and network configuration
Change the production controller settings to discover connected hosts

questions.explanation: The chapter warns that older controllers can crash under scans. It calls for drawings, switch and firewall records, provenance for each fact and joint follow-up on discrepancies.
